ledger.note: 4 June 1392: Charles VI creates the second dukedom of Orléans for his brother Louis. Page: 'The second dukedom of Orléans was created in 1392 by' Charles VI for his brother Louis; tenure from 4 June 1392. Crown lands page: 'Orléans appanage given to Louis I de Valois'. The Orléanais is my reading of the lands; the pages give no towns and no area.

23 November 1407: Louis of Orléans is murdered and his son Charles becomes duke. The page's table: Charles's tenure began 23 November 1407, the day Louis died, 'murdered by Duke of Burgundy's hitmen'.

ledger.note: 1498: the duchy merges into the crown when Louis XII is crowned. Crown lands page: the 1498 entry has 'Valois (alienated in 1386?) and Orléans (alienated in 1392) back to the royal domain'; the title page: Louis II's tenure ended 7 April 1498 '(Merged into the Crown titles)'.
1498: the Valois-Orléans duchy ends as a separate state. Valois and Orléans go 'back to the royal domain' (Crown lands page, 1498 entry).

certainty.note: An apanage with no boundary record on the pages.

sources.title: Duke of Orléans
sources.note: The article on the title: creations 1344, 1392, 1465; holders and tenures; seats Blois, Saint-Cloud, Palais-Royal; no lands or area.

sources.title: Crown lands of France
sources.note: 1392: Orléans appanage given to Louis I de Valois; 1498: the crowning of the new king brings his appanages back, with Valois (alienated in 1386?) and Orléans (alienated in 1392) back to the royal domain; the county of Blois is integrated into the royal domain for the first time.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from two pages (Duke of Orléans, Crown lands of France). The Duke of Orléans page is the article on the title: it gives creations, tenures and seats, and no lands, area or capital. The drawn land is the Orléanais region only. The Crown lands page's 1498 entry has Valois (alienated in 1386?) and Orléans (alienated in 1392) back in the domain; it says 'the county of Blois is integrated into the royal domain for the first time', so Blois is not a return and the page does not make it part of this duchy; Comminges (alienated in 1462) is a separate 1498 entry. Valois, Blois and Comminges are not drawn here (the royal-domain-of-france dossier draws Blois in 1498 from the last Cliopatria shape of the County of Blôis, 1395-1401). Charles of Orléans's captivity in England (1415-1440) and Asti, Coucy and Luxembourg are not on the pages.
The first dukedom (1344-1375, Philip of Valois) and the later creations (1550, 1626, 1661) are not drawn; the page gives them no lands. The dukedom is a separate state only while it was a great apanage; the Armagnac-Burgundian civil war article was not opened, so no war is listed (the title page names only the 1407 murder of Louis by the Duke of Burgundy's agents).
